subject: Follow-up: time-to-first-token targets and emission cadence for NuanceRetail pilot
summary: Post-discovery recap and technical qualification for NuanceRetail pilot focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) goals, streaming method (SSE preferred), chunk cadence targets, and capacity assumptions. Action items: confirm 95th percentile TTFT target, agree on pilot traffic profile, schedule engineering deep-dive + network trace handoff.
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana@nuanceretail.com>, Michael Cho <michael.cho@nuanceretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: time-to-first-token targets and emission cadence for NuanceRetail pilot

Thanks for taking the call today — great conversation. I wanted to capture the technical outcomes and next steps so we have a clear pilot acceptance bar and what engineering needs to validate next week. Key points from our discovery: 

- Goal (customer): deliver a responsive chat experience for retail agents and on-site kiosks; perceived interactivity is primary.
- TTFT target (proposed): 95th percentile <= 150 ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens). We agreed to test both 64-token and 256-token prompt profiles.
- Streaming method: you prefer Server-Sent Events (SSE) for browser kiosks; WebSocket supported as fallback in mobile/web SDKs.
- Chunk cadence: initial plan is 1st emission (prefix/first packet) within TTFT SLA, then subsequent chunks every ~60–90 ms for typical conversational outputs. We flagged that chunk frequency should be configurable per route.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state 120 rps, burst to 300 rps; concurrency estimate ~250–350 concurrent streams during peak.
- Fallbacks: in heavy load, we will route to a lower-cost model variant with degraded sampling settings; graceful degradation policy required.

Attachments: I attached an SLO matrix and a small prompt set we discussed. Please confirm the traffic profile (ratios of 64 vs 256 token prompts) and whether SSE is mandatory for kiosks.

Next steps (proposed):
1) NuanceRetail to send definitive traffic split and any NAT/proxy details by Mon 11/23.
2) Redwood to run an internal latency probe (p99/p95) on the chosen model variants and return a first-pass latency matrix by Tue 11/24.
3) Schedule an engineering deep-dive (30–45m) week of 11/30 — Karthik/Ben + Nuance infra/network lead.

If this matches your notes I’ll convert to a mutual action plan and open the pilot order.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — that matches our discussion. Couple clarifications from my side: 

- Traffic mix: start with 70% short prompts (~64 tokens), 25% mid (~256 tokens), 5% long (>512 tokens) during the pilot. We will provide a day-of-week and hourly spike profile with the NAT/proxy details by EOD today.
- SSE is required for the kiosk webview (we have limited WebSocket support on the legacy webview). Mobile apps will use WebSocket.
- For fallbacks, we can accept a lower-quality variant for kiosk sessions but want an explicit flag in the response to mark degraded generation so UX can show a subtle warning.

Also want to confirm what definition Redwood uses for TTFT — is it the time from request ingestion at your edge to the first token byte on the wire (not including client-side parse/render)?

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Senior Product Manager, NuanceRetail
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sana Patel <sana@nuanceretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Follow-up: time-to-first-token targets and emission cadence for NuanceRetail pilot

Thanks Sana — confirming definitions and a few tech notes so expectations are aligned: 

- Our TTFT definition: time from when the request fully arrives at Redwood's ingress (post any LB/NAT) to the first byte of the model output leaving our egress edge. That excludes client render time and client-side retry/backoff. We can instrument additional client-side timing if you want to capture end-to-end perceived latency.
- For 95th <= 150 ms at 70% short-profile, it is achievable on our M-class optimized variants with strategic prefix caching + 8-bit quantized kernels, assuming network RTT <= 40 ms and the request path does not traverse heavy proxy serialization.
- Chunk cadence: emitting subsequent chunks every 60–90 ms is fine as a target. Operationally we will expose a chunk-window config value per route (min cadence and max in-flight chunk size). For streaming we recommend SSE for kiosks as discussed; WebSocket will match behavior but has slightly different keep-alive characteristics.
- Capacity math: to hit 120 sustained rps with 300 burst we size pilot capacity for ~4 GPUs with per-GPU throughput assumptions (optimistic) — we will run a synthetic probe with your prompt set to confirm.

Action items for us:
- We will run a 1-hour probe (synthetic) against your NAT endpoint once you share the profile and network traces. Please attach your proxy/NAT logs and a representative trace.
- Karthik, Naomi: can you pick two available windows next week for the engineering deep-dive? Also flag any firewall rules for our IP ranges.

- One UX note: we can add a response header X-Redwood-Degraded: true when the fallback variant serves. Sana, confirm if that flag is OK for kiosk UX.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sana — thanks for the traffic split. Quick operational checklist from my side before the deep-dive: 

1) Please share a short pcap or single-flow trace that includes a representative kiosk session. We need path RTTs and any proxy TLS termination points.
2) Confirm whether kiosks sit behind a TLS-terminating CDN (e.g., Akamai/CloudFront) or direct NAT — this changes our edge placement.
3) For the engineering session, suggested slots (PST): Wed 11/24 10:00–10:45, Thu 11/25 14:00–14:45, or Mon 11/29 09:00–09:45. Pick one and we'll send a calendar invite.

For the pilot run: Ben and I will prepare two probe types:
- Latency probe: small-batch synthetic at ramped concurrency up to 350 concurrent streams; measure p50/p95/p99 TTFT and chunk cadence under steady state.
- Functional probe: sample prompt set through streaming path (SSE) and verify chunk boundaries and header flags (X-Redwood-Degraded).

We will also include a short checklist for the kiosk implementers so they can surface render latency separately (client-side paint).

I'll send invites once you confirm a slot and provide traces.

Karthik
Director, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
